newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-BROADHUST AND MARTIN BOOST RYDER PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BROADHUST AND MARTIN BOOST RYDER PROSPECTS.

text.p: England's Paul Broadhurst and Miguel Martin of Spain mastered cold and breezy conditions to give their Ryder Cup bids a small boost at Gut Kaden on Thursday.
The were a shot apart at the top of the leaderboard after the first round of the European Tournament Playuers Championship (TPC).

Broadhurst has had an indifferent few weeks since finishing second and third in the Cannes and Portuguese Opens but gave himself a start towards moving up from 10th in the European Ryder Cup by taking the lead with a four-under-par 68,

The 1991 Cup player had five birdies and just one bogey in tough conditions for a one-stroke lead over Martin, surprise package Alberto Binaghi of Italy and another former Ryder Cup man, England's Barry Lane.
Broadhurst's recent poor spell coincided with the birth of his third child.
"I don't want to use the birth as an excuse," said Broadhurst after beating tournament favourite Bernhard Langer, his playing-partner, by three shots.

"I didn't drive the ball great in Cannes even though I was second, and I've been trying to find a solution since. On Monday before the final round of the PGA I found something with my coach I could work on and though I didn't go into this round with much confidence, I gradually got it back.

"I'd been in a very good position for the Ryder Cup but lots of guys have gone mad over the past few weeks and overtaken me. It's very important to me and if I don't get in I'll feel as though I've blown it," Broadhurst said.
While Lane dropped a shot at 17 to enable Broadhurst to lead on his own, Martin birdied two of the last four holes, both par-fives, to sit just off the lead.
"I played very consistently bearing in mind the bad weather," said the Spaniard who put himself on the brink of his Cup debut by winning the Heineken Classic in Perth at the start of February.

"If I finish in the top five here I have a good chance for the Ryder Cup. I just try to do my best and if it comes along that's nice. If it doesn't then there is nothing I can do about it. But I'm playing good and all I need is a little bit of luck to get in."
Binaghi's 69 was in contrast to his noted compatriot Costantino Rocca's 78. Rocca is bidding for a third Ryder Cup appearance but suffered badly with his short game.
The Italian is seventh on the table and knows he must rediscover form quickly as others are overhauling him after he held a more promising position at the end of last year and the beginning of this.
Lane dropped a shot at the 17th to leave Broadhurst alone in front.

Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros shot a 77, finding the cold weather not good for his suspect back. "My chipping was poor, my putting was poor and my driving was poor. I had no confidence to gain any momentum," he said.
